newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvia c.bank head optimistic on banks, currency.
newsitem.headline: Latvia c.bank head optimistic on banks, currency.

text.p: Latvia's central bank head said on Wednesday the country's banking system was over the damaging crisis that hit it last year and the lat currency was stable.
"There are no hidden nasty surprises, at least according to our knowledge," central bank chief Einars Repshe told Reuters, speaking about the banking system.

Last year, Latvia was hit by one of the worst banking crises in eastern Europe when the closure of its top bank caused a chain reaction that shut several others. But the country has gradually recovered and confidence is returning.
"That bank crisis has passed...the core banks have fully recovered," Repshe added. He said some smaller banks may close or merge, but the current banking picture would change little.
The big three banks are privately-owned Riga Commercial Bank and Parex Bank plus formerly state-owned Unibanka.
Their assets total 403.7 million lats as of the end of September, and they hold deposits worth 301.1 million lats.
The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) has played a role in bringing stability, having taken stakes in Unibanka and Riga Commercial Bank.
Repshe also said that he foresaw no change to the country's lat currency, which is pegged at 0.7997 to the SDR.
Neighbouring country Lithuania is currently debating how to scrap its system of pegging its currency to the dollar.
"We are for stability and we have set up our regime and our traditions, and we will keep them," Repshe said.

He saw no need to consider a change. He said the time it may be a matter for debate could be if Latvia joined the European Union (EU). Latvia is queuing with other eastern European states for EU membership and hopes it may become a member between 2010-2015.
"How can there be stability if there are changes to the peg?" Repshe said.
